The chapter names him outright: "A number of ancient sites were excavated under the supervision of Sir Alexander Cunningham, the first Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India." So the answer is (a) Alexander Cunningham.

The near-miss is Sir John Marshall, who did head the ASI — the chapter says the Harappan Civilisation was discovered during his tenure — but he came later; the chapter reserves "first" for Cunningham. William Jones founded the Asiatic Society in Kolkata in 1784 and Friedrich Max Muller was an Orientalist scholar of Sanskrit; the chapter connects neither of them to the Archaeological Survey.

The chapter states it directly of Friedrich Max Muller: "He first translated the Sanskrit text of 'Hitopadesh' in German language." So the answer is (b) Friedrich Max Muller. The chapter also credits him with translating the Rigveda into German, which confirms him as the scholar it associates with German translation.

Of the others, the chapter says James Mill wrote 'The History of British India' (published 1817) and Mountstuart Elphinstone wrote 'The History of India' (1841) — works they authored, not translations from Sanskrit — and Sir John Marshall is named in the chapter only as an archaeologist.
